subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap

Hi Chris,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps so everyone is aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High/variable latency on search/QA path for short queries (~300-500ms today).
- Inconsistent retrieval relevancy from current embeddings -> manual reranking required.
- Need for structured outputs (invoice fields, product attributes) for downstream systems.
- Compliance: some PII must remain in your VPC; interested in Private deployment options.

Goals we discussed:
- Latency target: <200ms median for short interactive queries.
- Improve semantic search precision by ~10-20% via embeddings + reranking.
- Expose structured, function-callable outputs for downstream ingestion (JSON schema).
- 2-week POC to validate integration and SLOs.

Integration notes / fit (technical):
- SDK: Redwood provides streaming responses and function-calling helpers. For structured outputs we'll use function-calling to return JSON payloads that map to your ingestion schema.
- Embeddings/reranking: run embeddings on your document set, use our local reranker (candidate scoring + model rerank) in the retrieval loop.
- Streaming: we can stream incremental tokens for the UI to reduce perceived latency; backend will use prefix caching and batching to keep cost predictable.
- Auth/Network: for the POC we can use API tokens scoped to a test project; for production we can discuss SSO + VPC/private deployment.

Attachments: postcall-deck.pdf (two-slide summary), integration-mockup.png (example function schema).

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive (Dev + Chris + Redwood infra) — 60m. Suggested window: Thu/ Fri next week.
2) Dev to share sample dataset & QPS expectations.
3) Redwood to spin up a POC project (2 weeks) and provide success criteria template.
4) Michael to send indicative pricing and options (Hosted vs Dedicated).

Chris — can you confirm the sample dataset location and whether we should expect peak QPS ~50 or more during the POC? Also confirm if we should coordinate with your SSO admin for temporary test accounts.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first inference platform
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and action items. Couple quick clarifications: 

- Sample dataset: I've uploaded a representative dump to S3: https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/sample-dataset.csv (contains ~120k doc rows; fields: id, text, metadata). We can provide a smaller 10k subset if needed for quicker testing.
- QPS: For the POC keep expectations low — peak simulated QPS ~30, avg 8-12. Production could be higher but we want to validate behavior first.
- Function calling: we'll need structured output for invoice extraction (fields: invoice_id, vendor, total_amount, tax, due_date). I'll attach a sample schema later.
- SSO: our SSO admin is sso-admin@acme.com — they can create test accounts or we can provide short-lived API creds.

Can we target Fri 2027-04-09 for the technical deep-dive? That works for our team in the morning PST.

Appreciate the quick turnaround here.

—Chris
Chris Nolan
Head of Search & Discovery, Acme Corp
chris.nolan@acme.com
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap — technical questions

Hi Chris — looping in a few technical follow-ups so we can scope the POC precisely.

Thanks for the S3 link — I grabbed a sample subset. A few questions: 
1) Data format: is the CSV text column normalized (HTML stripped) or should we expect noisy markup? Any PII tagging in metadata?
2) Embedding size: currently we plan to use our 1536-dim embedding profile for semantic recall; are you tied to a particular vector size?
3) Reranking: do you want the reranker to run on top-K candidates (we typically do top-100 -> rerank top-10) or prefer a lighter approach?
4) Function calling schema: can you share the exact JSON schema for invoice extraction? Our function-calling templates will validate against it and we can provide an example mapping (see attached: integration-mockup.png).
5) QPS & concurrency: you mentioned peak ~30 QPS — is that sustained or short spikes? Any SLA targets we should know about for 95th/99th p50 latencies?

Technical notes on our side:
- SDK: for the POC please use redwood-js v1.7.0 (we'll provide a temporary token). This supports streaming responses via the "stream()" helper and built-in function-calling wrappers that return validated JSON.
- Structured outputs: we can return either (a) function-call JSON (recommended) which your ingest pipeline can consume directly, or (b) streaming text plus post-parse. Function calling lowers parsing errors.
- Reranking: we can include a small learned reranker model as part of the POC; it runs locally in the runtime to keep latencies low.

If you can share the JSON schema and confirm whether we should provision a VPC endpoint for data locality during the POC, I can scope the infra work and give a timeline.

Thanks — Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap — pricing/POC options

Chris — quick note on pricing and options so you have something to consider before the deep-dive.

Options for a 2-week POC:
1) Hosted POC (fastest): temporary project, usage-based billing. Estimated cost for test volume (10-30 QPS, embeddings + rerank) ~ $3k-$6k for the POC period.
2) Dedicated POC (reserved nodes): if you want more predictable latencies and private networking for the POC, we can provision a small dedicated pool — estimated cost ~$6k-$10k for the 2-week window (one-time).

We can keep the POC scoped to Hosted and then migrate to Dedicated if you require VPC controls. After the POC, if you choose Redwood Dedicated or Private we'll include migration assistance.

I'll prepare a short one-page statement of work and a DocuSign link for approval if you'd like to fast-track (link: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/ACME-POC). No obligation — just to give you options.

Best,
Michael Grant
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
From: Chris Nolan <chris.nolan@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: sso-admin@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-05T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sales discovery: Redwood integration recap — next steps confirmed

Thanks all — quick confirmations: 
- Tech deep-dive: Fri 2027-04-09 at 09:30 PST confirmed. I'll forward calendar invites.
- POC start: we can start the POC on Mon 2027-04-12.
- Sample data: full dataset link (read-only): https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/sample-dataset.csv. For the POC use the 10k subset I placed at https://acme.s3.amazonaws.com/sample-dataset-subset-10k.csv to speed things up.
- SSO: looped in sso-admin@acme.com for account creation — they will provision a test user and let you know next steps.

Dev — invoice JSON schema will be attached in a follow-up (I will drop the schema into the calendar event). Michael — the hosted POC cost looks fine; we can go that route for the initial test and evaluate Dedicated after results.

Attachment: sso-invite.png (screenshot of the SSO invite email).

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Chris
